brief: Bad vs Good vs Great prompts — what changes as you climb each tier.

slots.body: Bad prompts demand blindly. Good ones ask clearly. Great prompts wrap the task in role, audience, and constraints first.
slots.note: Context reduces hallucination and aligns tone instantly.

slots.body: Bad prompts cram everything into one sentence. Good prompts list requirements. Great prompts sequence reasoning so the model checks itself.
slots.note: Step-by-step structures outperform flat instructions every time.

slots.body: Bad prompts leave output shape to chance. Good ones mention format. Great prompts provide a template or example to fill verbatim.
slots.note: Examples beat descriptions when precision matters.

slots.body: Bad prompts ignore length and style. Good prompts add a constraint or two. Great prompts define what to avoid as clearly as what to include.
slots.note: Negative constraints cut fluff faster than positive ones.

slots.body: Bad prompts accept the first draft. Good prompts ask for revision. Great prompts build in a critique loop where the model scores its own answer.
slots.note: Meta-cognition turns decent answers into exceptional ones.

slots.body: Bad prompts treat the model like a search engine. Good ones assign a job title. Great prompts flesh out expertise, bias, and voice.
slots.note: A vivid persona unlocks latent knowledge in the weights.

slots.body: Save this framework and test it on your next prompt. Great results come from great structure.
